observations: Silver-colored microwave oven with a digital control panel.
The control panel includes a rotary dial and six buttons.
The brand logo in the top left corner is illegible due to low resolution.
The text on the buttons and display is blurry and unreadable.
The unit appears to be stacked on or next to other appliances, suggesting a commercial or storage environment.
A small white sticker is visible on the top right corner of the door.

claims.evidence: The buttons are too blurry to confirm a 'Grill' function, though the layout is consistent with grill models.

claims.claim: Barely used, bought new last year
claims.evidence: This contradicts the 'London used' claim, as 'London used' typically refers to imported second-hand goods.
Microwaves do not have a 'motor' in the sense of an engine; this likely refers to the internal components or magnetron.

risks.risk: Magnetron failure (unit runs but does not heat)
risks.proof: A video showing the microwave heating a cup of water to boiling point.
A photo of the interior top element glowing or a video of it in grill mode.
A clear photo of the interior cavity with the door open.
A clear photo of the manufacturer's specification plate on the back of the unit.

proof_requests: Clear photo of the specification plate on the back showing brand, model, and capacity.
Clear photo of the front control panel and brand logo.
Photo of the interior cavity with the door open.
Video of the unit heating water and the grill element functioning.
Photo of the mentioned receipt and warranty card.
response.reason: The brand, model, and capacity are unreadable in the single blurry photo provided, making it impossible to determine a baseline value. Furthermore, the seller's claims are contradictory, describing the item as both 'London used' (second-hand import) and 'bought new last year'.
